description: This bar chart illustrates the number of samples used for different reasoning categories in a dataset. The horizontal axis displays the reasoning categories: Mathematical, General, Natural Scene, Physical Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Logical Puzzle, and Chemical Reasoning, listed in descending order based on sample count. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10<sup>2</sup> to 10<sup>4</sup>, with tick labels at intervals of 10<sup>2</sup>, 10<sup>3</sup>, and 10<sup>4</sup>.  A single set of light blue bars represents the sample count for each category; the tallest bar corresponds to “Mathematical” reasoning with a value of 7025, while the shortest bar represents “Chemical Reasoning” with a value of 49.  The bar for “General” reasoning has a value of 1709, “Natural Scene” has a value of 413, “Physical Reasoning” has a value of 232, “Logical Reasoning” has a value of 91, and “Logical Puzzle” has a value of 49. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
